tradeoffs.observed: EditFormFieldUseCase declares optionRepo as an optional constructor dependency and returns an empty options array without persisting when optionRepo is omitted.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Preserves backwards compatibility for existing call sites and unit tests initialized without optionRepo. Risks silent drop of field choices when options are submitted to a use case instance lacking the repository.

options.gains: Avoids breaking existing unit tests and instantiations that omit optionRepo.
options.costs: Permits silent persistence omission if a caller passes options to an unconfigured use case instance.

options.gains: Guarantees that every use case instance has an option persistence implementation when handling fields.
options.costs: Requires updating all existing use case instantiations and unit test suites to pass a mock or concrete option repository.

tradeoffs.question: Under what conditions should EditFormFieldUseCase require optionRepo as a mandatory dependency versus allowing an optional parameter?

tradeoffs.observed: TerminalLogger.debug unconditionally writes formatted logs to stdout via console.log on every call, including each Repository database operation.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Gives immediate visual timing and query confirmation in terminal outputs during development. Adds continuous stdout stream overhead and log volume during high-concurrency database interactions.

options.gains: Guarantees full query visibility and timing without needing environment configuration.
options.costs: Generates continuous stdout output on every repository database operation regardless of environment.

options.gains: Suppresses debug log emission in production or test runs unless an explicit flag is enabled.
options.costs: Requires defining and checking a log level configuration or environment flag before printing.

tradeoffs.question: How should debug-level database logs be gated between development inspection and high-throughput execution?

tradeoffs.observed: getEncryptionKey falls back to a hardcoded string secret when FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY* and BETTER_AUTH_SECRET environment variables are unset.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Enables zero-config local testing and development workflows without requiring environment variable bootstrapping. Risks silent deployment with well-known cryptographic keys if production configurations omit secrets.

options.gains: Allows tests and local runtimes to start without environment configuration.
options.costs: Risks encrypting sensitive production data with a shared default key if secrets are missing.

options.gains: Ensures production environments fail fast if encryption keys are absent.
options.costs: Requires environment detection logic (e.g. NODE_ENV === "production") inside the key resolution utility.

tradeoffs.question: Under what deployment conditions should cryptographic key resolution fail fast rather than falling back to default keys?

tradeoffs.observed: withoutDeletedAt strips the database deletedAt timestamp from entity records before returning them from repository CRUD operations.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Isolates soft-delete implementation details inside the database package so domain entities do not carry database lifecycle fields. Prevents repository callers from inspecting when a record was deleted when building audit views without separate queries.

options.gains: Keeps domain entity contracts decoupled from storage-level soft-delete mechanics.
options.costs: Hides deletion timestamps from standard repository callers.

options.gains: Exposes explicit audit or historical query methods on the repository when deletion metadata is required.
options.costs: Adds separate query methods and return types alongside the standard BaseRepository interface.

tradeoffs.question: How should entities distinguish between domain-facing records and soft-delete audit records when deletion history is required?

tradeoffs.observed: FormField replaces an untyped JSON config property with explicit typed attributes (placeholder, min, max, minLength, maxLength, options).
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Replaces unstructured JSON with schema-enforced, type-safe fields and database-level constraints. Any dynamic properties previously accommodated in config that lack a dedicated column must now be formally added to the schema.

options.gains: Enforces strict typing and database column mappings across all field validations.
options.costs: Requires explicit schema migrations whenever new field attributes are needed.

options.gains: Allows arbitrary custom field properties without schema migrations while keeping common attributes typed.
options.costs: Maintains dual property storage (columns vs metadata bag) and complicates validation logic.

tradeoffs.question: How should future field type configurations be accommodated between first-class entity properties and dynamic metadata?

resolved.resolution: Implemented fail-fast checks in getEncryptionKey and getLookupKey when NODE_ENV is production.
Gated debug-level log emission behind NODE_ENV/DEBUG and LOG_LEVEL filters.
Guarded against silent option omission by throwing InternalError if options are passed without optionRepo.
Restored explicit : never return type annotation on throwAppError in error.ts.
